stem: Which model can best be used to justify why the formula for the area of a triangle is \( \frac{1}{2}bh \)?

options.label: A
options.text: (Image of triangle with base \(b\) and height \(h\) transforming to a smaller triangle with dimensions labeled \( \frac{1}{2}b \) and \( \frac{1}{2}h \))

options.label: B
options.text: (Image of triangle with base \(b\) and height \(h\) transforming to a triangle with lines dividing into three smaller sections with right angles, all labeled with base \(b\))

options.label: C
options.text: (Image of triangle with base \(b\) and height \(h\) transforming to a parallelogram composed of two copies of the original triangle, with base \(b\) and height \(h\))

options.label: D
options.text: (Image of triangle with base \(b\) and height \(h\) transforming to two triangles stacked vertically, each with base \(b\) and height \(h\))

visual_elements: Images of triangles showing geometric transformations to illustrate area calculation
